requirements.title: AI transfer and declaration procedure
requirements.summary: Current Engineering students, including first- and second-year M&T students, may apply by submitting a four-year academic plan and the Declare/Update Field of Study form. Other students must follow the Engineering transfer policy, which remains inaccessible in this review.

requirements.title: Graduation limit for changing into AI
requirements.summary: The major change is not approved unless graduation remains possible within eight total semesters, or ten for M&T students.

requirements.title: Dual majors and other degrees
requirements.summary: Engineering dual majors are permitted except CSCI, NETS and SSE. Eligibility for dual degrees or College of Arts and Sciences second majors, including VIPER, requires program advising review.

requirements.title: Incoming M&T declaration timing
requirements.summary: Incoming first-year M&T students may begin declaring AI on the first day of their first fall semester using the field-of-study form.

requirements.title: Scope of the linked technical-elective list
requirements.summary: The CIS handbook explicitly allows its approved technical-elective entries in ARIN. Its subsequent restricted-course quotas concern the 37-CU CSCI degree and are not applied here. The AI program separately permits Engineering, Mathematics and Natural Science courses.

requirements.title: Technical electives requiring individual approval
requirements.summary: These entries are marked ask and are not included as automatically approved options. Seek the CIS undergraduate chair’s decision with supporting documentation before counting one.

notes: The program webpage is undated and is not assigned a catalog year. The catalog URL returned an empty response; program-page evidence supports the record.

The overview says students choose a concentration, but the explicit AI Concentrations section says concentrations are optional and use four of the six AI elective courses. This inconsistency is unresolved.
Course options may appear in several categories. Listed pools must not be summed; this record does not assert double-counting permission.

CIS 3200 public archive and Fall 2021 HTML course outline verified 2026-10-10 (penn-cis3200-archive; penn-cis3200-fall-2021-outline). The official CIS 3200 archive links this older CIS 320-numbered offering. Syllabus URL is an example HTML outline with topics, prerequisites and grading, not a PDF or evidence of current offering/requirements. Current curriculum source_id is unchanged.

Inferred taxonomy labels summarize themes evidenced by the cited curriculum sections, including elective options where stated. They are analyst classifications, not institution-stated learning outcomes or guarantees that every student completes every theme. Source-stated outcomes are retained separately.

All eight primary curriculum accordions observed, including optional concentration pools. Linked approved lists, college-wide completion rules, and the overview/concentration inconsistency remain unresolved; degree curriculum stays partial. Individual course metadata are separate and are not inferred from section totals.

Program-page titles differ for some optional concentration codes and the main elective pool; a shared course record retains the main-pool title. Optional pool membership does not automatically authorize use outside the AI Elective category. Transfer timing and dual-major restrictions in the FAQ require further structured review.

2026-10-10 linked technical-elective review: 351 current approved entries and 13 ask entries mapped from the official JSON. The handbook explicitly extends approved entries to ARIN; the subsequent restricted-course quota belongs to 37-CU CSCI and is not imposed on AI.

AI FAQ transfer/declaration, eight-semester (ten for M&T) limit, dual-major exclusions, and incoming M&T declaration timing are mapped. Full Engineering transfer and degree policies remain blocked by cross-origin robots redirect.
STAT 4300 title was verified through the official technical-elective inventory; individual units and prerequisites remain unknown.
